title: Every agent writes the context in the chat before it asks — never 'read it on the board'
description: Add one explicit rule wherever the agent asks the human something: before any question for decide, approve or accept, write the full context in this conversation — the decision's options with reason and costLater, or the whole approach and every acceptance criterion, or the review findings. Never replace it with a pointer to the board, the dashboard or `sober` CLI; the board is a second copy, not the only one. Sources: plugins/skills/{decide,brief,next,plan,loop}/SKILL.md (edit the source, then `pnpm plugins` regenerates packages/*-plugin skills), the server instructions in packages/mcp/src/index.ts:29, and the decide/approve/accept descriptions in packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts and review.ts. Under tool-renders/both, the rule says 'paste the block the tool returned'. Test: a check (in the existing plugin build/drift test) that each of those skills contains the rule sentence; `pnpm plugins` leaves no diff.

brief.approach:
Score 4: prose in seven places plus a drift check. No logic — which is why the whole risk is wording that varies between the copies and so stops being recognisable.

**One sentence, written once, repeated verbatim.** Decide the exact words first and use them everywhere; a rule phrased three ways is three rules. Something in the file's own register: *Before you ask, write the whole thing in this conversation — never a pointer to the board, the dashboard or the CLI.* The accepted decision is "tool renders it and the instructions require it", and the tool half landed with `the-brief-the-options-and-the-review-com-uwco`: `write_brief` now returns the rendered brief, and `renderDecisions` and `renderReview` each end with `Paste this above the question before you ask.` So the instruction half says **paste the block the tool returned** — it must point at that block by name, or the two halves drift into two different asks.

**The seven places.**

- `plugins/skills/decide/SKILL.md` — before the pick: every option with its `reason` and its `costLater`, not a summary of them. ADR 0024 makes those two the education pillar; a pointer to the board deletes it.
- `plugins/skills/brief/SKILL.md` — before the approval: the whole approach and every acceptance criterion.
- `plugins/skills/next/SKILL.md` — it walks brief → approve → run → review → accept, so it carries the rule at both the approval and the accept, and at the accept the review's findings go in the chat.
- `plugins/skills/plan/SKILL.md` and `plugins/skills/loop/SKILL.md` — one line each, where they hand off to a question.
- `packages/mcp/src/index.ts:29`, the server `instructions` string — one clause added to the sentence that already says picking, approving and accepting are the human's. This reaches every host whether or not it installed a skill, so it is the one that matters most.
- The `decide`, `approve` and `accept` tool `description`s in `packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts` and `packages/mcp/src/tools/review.ts` — each already tells the agent to ask with the host's own question tool (ADR 0057); add the clause that the context goes in the chat first. Note `approve`'s description was extended by `approve-asks-once-drop-the-leftover-asky-9818`; read it and add to it rather than rewriting it.

Then `pnpm plugins` and commit the generated `packages/*-plugin` skills with the source. Never hand-edit a generated copy.

**The check.** `test/integration/plugin.test.ts` already asserts the generated skills match their source. Add one case there: each of the five skill sources contains the rule sentence. Assert on one distinctive fragment of it — the whole sentence as a string constant in the test, compared against each file — so rewording the rule fails the test and forces the person to reword all five. That is the only thing keeping seven copies in step, and the accepted decision's cost line names exactly this as what has to be maintained.

**Do not** add a runtime check that an agent actually pasted anything. There is nothing to observe: the conversation is the host's, not SOBER's. The mechanism is the tool returning the block and the prose requiring it, and that is the decision.

Nothing else changes: no core, no schema, no CLI, no dashboard, no server route.

acceptance.proves: all five skill sources carry the rule word for word and the four generated copies of each match after `pnpm plugins` — rewording it in one place now fails the build instead of silently drifting

acceptance.run: for f in decide brief next plan loop; do grep -qi 'never a pointer\|in this conversation' plugins/skills/$f/SKILL.md || { echo "$f is missing the rule"; exit 1; }; done && echo all five
acceptance.proves: every skill that leads to a question carries it — not only the two where a human is asked most often

acceptance.run: git grep -qi 'conversation' -- packages/mcp/src/index.ts && git grep -qi 'conversation' -- packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts packages/mcp/src/tools/review.ts
acceptance.proves: the rule reaches a host that installed no skill at all, through the server instructions and the three tool descriptions

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'Paste this above the question before you ask' -- packages/mcp/src
acceptance.proves: the tool half the instructions point at is still there — the prose says paste the block the tool returned, and a rule naming a block that does not exist is worse than no rule
this is prose and its drift check only: no core, no schema, no CLI, no dashboard, no server route
the widened description and instruction strings compile
